text:
nina: Heads-up from onboarding: rolled canary for aurora-48k-int3 with streaming + function_call enabled. Running longprefill smoke and seeing reproducible KV-desync when a function call token span appears near rotary wrap boundaries (~23.5k). Output resumes with repeated 2-4 token loops after the function call returns.

rashid: can you paste the minimal repro and the stream headers? curious if this is prefetch vs streaming ordering.

nina: minimal curl (streaming): ```bash
curl -s -N -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/v1/stream \
  -d '{"model":"aurora-48k-int3","input":"A"*23488+"\nCALL: get_state()","max_tokens":64,"prefetch_kv":true,"stream":true}'
```
stream event sample shows: `event: token stream; token_pos=23492; kv_write=slot=5:idx=1023` then immediately after function call return we see `event: token stream; token_pos=23493; kv_write=slot=5:idx=1023` again and generation repeats.

sam: that looks like the writer didn't advance the handshake cursor across the function-call boundary. Did the function-call handler buffer tokens and publish them out of band? opsbot: any recent deploys touching streaming writer or function-call batching?

opsbot: Deployed canary aurora-48k-int3 (deploy id: dply-20260326-14). No separate function-call changes in this deploy. Recent PR abcdef modified streaming writer to batch small writes for throughput.

rashid: hypothesis: streaming writer batches tokens written during function-call handling and replays them to the prefetch writer without updating the rot_index->slot mapping after RoPE rebase. At large contexts RoPE rebase (scaled LUT) changes the slot_base computation; if writer replays stale slot values we see repeats.

nina: I dumped handshake rows across the function-call boundary: ```
# token_pos -> (rot_block, slot, kv_idx)
23490 -> (11, 1021, 4090)
23491 -> (11, 1022, 4091)
23492 -> (11, 1023, 4092)
-- function call => handler runs, emits stored tokens --
23493 -> (11, 1023, 4092) <-- repeated write
23494 -> (12, 0, 4093)
```

sam: yep repeated kv_idx at the exact wrap point. Two possible root causes: (A) writer batches precomputed pack words and reuses them after RoPE recalculation, or (B) function-call handler uses a different rope_index fn (legacy) when re-serializing tokens.

rashid: quick local test: toggling `STREAM_BATCHER_DISABLE=1` removes the repeat. Also `ROPE_CTL=legacy` removes it. So it's the interaction of batcher + scaled rope.

nina: agreed. next steps proposed: (1) add a small unit that simulates out-of-band token emission (function call) at rotary wrap boundaries and asserts monotonic kv_idx; (2) change stream batcher to recompute slot/pack just before enqueueing to prefetch writer (cheap re-encode), or add a lightweight sequence number so stale pack words are detected and skipped; (3) add onboarding smoke that includes function-call injection cases for large windows.

sam: I'll whip up the unit + small patch to recompute before enqueue. We'll gate with `STREAM_SAFE_REENCODE=1` to measure perf. If perf cost negligible we can flip.

rashid: also add an eval that compares top-1 token continuity pre/post function call over 1000 samples; fail canary if repeat rate > 0.5% in boundary bins.

nina: thanks. I'll run an overnight sweep with `STREAM_SAFE_REENCODE=1` and post heatmap + small trace. Ops, please schedule a canary once PR lands.

opsbot: Deploy plan created: aurora-48k-stream-reencode (plan id: plan-20260326-55).
